status_summary: EO 14170 (90 FR 8621, signed 2025-01-20) directed a Federal Hiring Plan using technical and alternative assessments and an 80-day time-to-hire target. OPM's Merit Hiring Plan of 2025-05-29 requires at least one technical or alternative assessment in every competitive hiring process, bars self-assessments for rating or ranking, and strongly encourages USA Hire (135 job series). OPM ended agency use of the ACWA assessment by guidance in early 2026, pointing to USA Hire. EO 14281 (2025-04-23) told agencies to deprioritize disparate-impact enforcement and review consent judgments, and following a 2026-06-09 DOJ Office of Legal Counsel opinion OPM issued an interim final rule (91 FR 48234, effective 2026-07-31, comments closed 2026-09-29) removing Uniform Guidelines references from its regulations. The status of the PACE-era consent decree and of the Guidelines at other agencies was not verified.

timeline.event: EO 14170 directs a Federal Hiring Plan: technical and alternative assessments, time-to-hire under 80 days, and senior-leader involvement in hiring.

EO 14281 sets a policy of ending disparate-impact liability to the extent possible, directs agencies to deprioritize its enforcement, and orders review of existing consent judgments and injunctions that rely on it.

OPM and the Domestic Policy Council issue the Merit Hiring Plan: every competitive hiring process must include at least one technical or alternative assessment before a certificate issues, self-assessments may no longer be used for rating or ranking, and agencies are strongly encouraged to use USA Hire validated assessments (135 job series); short essay questions are added (guidance 2025-06-23, updated 2026-04-30).
OPM announces the Rule of Many, replacing the rule of three and category rating so agencies can select from a wider group of top candidates ranked by skills-based assessments.
OPM issues guidance telling agencies to stop using the Administrative Careers with America assessment after 36 years, pointing to validated tools such as USA Hire (date from OPM's news listing).

OPM interim final rule (91 FR 48234, RIN 3206-AP20) removes Uniform Guidelines references from 5 CFR 300.103(c), 330.213 and 337.303 and removes 720.206, citing a 2026-06-09 DOJ OLC opinion; job-analysis and nondiscrimination requirements remain. Comments closed 2026-09-29.

OPM publishes an interim rule on shared certificates and pooled hiring (91 FR 58347, effective 2026-10-15), citing a governmentwide goal OPM set through guidance that at least 60 percent of external competitive-service selections in FY2027 come from shared certificates.
OPM time-to-hire memo encourages validated skills-based assessments early in hiring and sets an 80-calendar-day overall standard.

title: Restore skills-based hiring tests and narrow disparate-impact limits on selection
uncertainties: Not verified: whether the Luevano-era consent decree was modified or terminated (OPM's ACWA release says ACWA was developed in response to that decree, but does not address the decree's status); whether EEOC, DOJ or Labor changed their parts of the Uniform Guidelines (29 CFR 1607 and related), which the OPM interim final rule does not address; and how widely agencies now use USA Hire. The Merit Hiring Plan PDF was read in full in review and states no fiscal-year assessment target; the FY2027 external-hire assessment target formerly listed could not be located, and the only FY2027 goal found is OPM's shared-certificate goal cited in the 2026-09-15 interim rule. The Merit Hiring Plan also includes four short essay questions for applicants (guidance 2025-06-23, updated 2026-04-30); their content was not read, and the Mandate does not mention essay questions. The ACWA release page shows no date, so 2026-02-25 comes from OPM's news listing. EO 14281 and the OLC opinion were not reread in this review. The Mandate speaks of USAHire as a testing model; OPM's description of USA Hire as validated assessments is taken from its own pages.
